subject: API auth & key management for FinServ integration - postcall recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Wright <samuel.wright@finserv.io>, Claire Jiang <c.jiang@finserv.io>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-25T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: API auth & key management (FinServ)

Hi Samuel / Claire —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of ask:
- You want to integrate Redwood for embeddings + reranking and model generation for customer-facing features.
- Key concerns: secure server-to-server auth for API calls, rotating keys, per-tenant isolation, and minimising scope for front-end flows.

Notes from call:
- FinServ will run inference calls from your backend (server-hosted) and some limited browser-based calls for demo UIs.
- You prefer not to store long-lived API keys in your production backend without rotation or KMS-backed secrets.
- Compliance team will want rotation policy and audit logs (SOC2 scope).

Recommendations (initial):
1) Server-to-server: use service accounts + short-lived JWTs (recommended). Create a per-environment service account in your infra that exchanges credentials for a Redwood short-lived token (we support token TTLs as low as 15m).
2) Key rotation: manage signing keys in your KMS (Vault/GCP KMS/Azure KeyVault) and rotate primary signing key on a scheduled cadence (we recommend 90 days for rotation + immediate revocation support).
3) Browser flows: do NOT embed long-lived API keys. Instead, issue ephemeral tokens from your backend for demo UIs with limited scopes and TTLs.
4) Least privilege: use granular routes/policies (embedding-only vs generation) and per-route quotas to limit blast radius.

Attachments: I’ve attached our SDK quickstart and a short security-sheet that outlines implementation patterns.

Next steps:
- I’ll loop in our infra lead (Dylan) to map the exchange flow and sample code snippets.
- Share a mutual action plan and a sandbox org for you to test token exchange.
- Schedule a security deep-dive with our compliance engineer — proposed window next week.

Would you prefer Tues 8/31 or Wed 9/1 for the security call?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf; redwood-security-sheet.pdf

Thanks Marissa — super helpful summary. A few clarifying questions from our side before we bring infra & security in: 

1) Can you confirm whether Redwood supports short-lived JWTs that are verifiable by your gateway (i.e., we sign with our KMS and you accept the JWT without us sharing private keys)?
2) For embeddings: does Redwood support tenant-scoped API keys or service accounts so we can ensure embeddings from FinServ are logically partitioned?
3) Is there an out-of-the-box rotation workflow (e.g., old keys automatically invalidated) or do we need to build a key-exchange/rolling system on our side?
4) Any sample Node/Go SDK code for the exchange flow (backend issues token -> frontend uses ephemeral token)?

Attaching a short doc with our internal questions. Happy to have a quick bridge with your infra folks.

Sam

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-26T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: API auth & key management (FinServ)

Samuel — looping in Dylan (infra lead) and Dev (security/SDK) to answer the technical Qs and propose a concrete flow. See inline responses below.

On your questions: 

> 1) Can you confirm whether Redwood supports short-lived JWTs that are verifiable by your gateway (i.e., we sign with our KMS and you accept the JWT without us sharing private keys)?

- Dylan: Yes — we support signed JWTs where you use your KMS to sign a keypair and exchange the public key with us. We verify signatures and issue a Redwood session token. We also support mutual TLS for additional assurance if desired.

> 2) For embeddings: does Redwood support tenant-scoped API keys or service accounts so we can ensure embeddings from FinServ are logically partitioned?

- Dev: We support per-organization service accounts and per-project scopes. You can provision a service account that only has embeddings & rerank permissions and routes traffic to an isolated storage namespace. We also offer per-tenant model routing if you want to pin different model variants.

> 3) Is there an out-of-the-box rotation workflow (e.g., old keys automatically invalidated) or do we need to build a key-exchange/rolling system on our side?

- Dylan: Redwood supports key revocation & versioning on our side. For full automation we recommend combining KMS key rotation with a short-lived JWT exchange. That way you rotate your signing keys in KMS, generate new pubkeys on our control plane, and we accept tokens signed by the active key. We will provide scripts and CI/CD snippets to automate the exchange.

> 4) Any sample Node/Go SDK code for the exchange flow (backend issues token -> frontend uses ephemeral token)?

- Dev: Attached is a short code snippet (see SDK quickstart). High level:
  - Backend: sign a JWT with subject set to your service account + requested scopes -> POST /v1/auth/exchange -> get back a short-lived Redwood token.
  - Frontend: call your backend to request ephemeral token (scoped, TTL 5-15m) -> use token to call embeddings/generation endpoints.

Next suggested steps from our side:
- Dylan & Dev to run a 45m technical session to map the exchange flow and walk through SDK snippets.
- I’ll provision a sandbox org and create a service account for FinServ with embeddings-only scope.
- Security call: proposed Tue 2026-08-31 10:00am PT (we can adjust).

Dylan / Dev — can you confirm availability for the technical session and whether you want access details or a repo for code samples?

Thanks — Marissa
